review_method: Same ChatGPT context, second failure-oriented inspection of original image after immutable first-reader draft freeze. Distinct adversarial purpose, NOT isolated blind second reader or independent third reviewer. No original embedded PDF OCR or peer source used. Any plausible errors remain unresolved and first response unchanged.

source_spot_checks.image_evidence: Printed Roman folio L at upper left, distinct from scan index 59.
First 9 printed rows continue printed comparison of Cherubim and life tree, with dense early-Cyrillic quote and end reference (161—162).
Next block introduces physiological discussion and old Cyrillic reproductive text; print changes font within physical rows.
Latin quote on physiological hot/cold theory, continuing over several source physical lines with spaced author name and bibliographic imprint.
Cain and Abel quotation with printed [sic!] and bibliography in same paragraph, no clean separate region boundary.
Final 12 physical rows begin with printed section titles, include dense old-Cyrillic genealogy and end mid-word 'Ме-' above lower blank margin.

additional_adversarial_observations.source_evidence: The printed physical line begins in a previous source passage; never invent its opening from I/58.
The printed opening old-Cyrillic question has bracketed material and appears to use historic type with difficult spacing. The draft word Разумѣеши needs crop.
The first-reader ѡстѫпи may hide different original consonants/vowels; physical line coverage is not text accuracy.
The sequence 'Іс҃у и ѧвѣ пронзи ка-' is a high-probability substantive misreading. Require second full-source reading rather than philological correction.
The phrase 'Гн҃а кровъ ... очисти ю и ѡсти' may contain fabricated or omitted letters, retain only as tentative first response.
Editorial brackets [ѡ], [во] and divine references cannot be inferred from a parallel edition.
The `ѡ зачатїи Каїна` heading appears inline within Franko prose; don't manufacture new physical lines or verified section nodes.
The embryo/genesis old-script words are compressed, with source letterform uncertainty for every word.
The end-of-line hyphen following смерзъ- must not be removed by normalization.
Latin original starts at end of the Cyrillic prose line after `quod`; printed quote should be rechecked for punctuation.
Complete Latin sentence is visibly present but exact letters/periods should be proofed directly. Do not treat background knowledge as facsimile.
The Latin quote continues and ends before spaced author citation `Albertus`; source quote boundary important.
Print has bibliographic imprint `Amsterodami 1660` and `p. 17—18`, but citation is not independently verified.
The odd phrase `Дегенши [Диоген?]` is a dangerous hypothesis, perhaps materially inconsistent with the print; don't upgrade to verified.
Original `[sic!]` is explicit editorial text, while surrounding old-Cyrillic phrase could contain multiple errors.
The heading `ѡ души и ѡ разѫме` contains source historic overmarks that may be omitted in plain Unicode.
A proposed `г҃. с҃ны` expression has uncertain numeral/titla; no morphological normalization.
The Eve name as `Евзе` appears especially doubtful; revisit original, not lexicon.
The Abel slaying phrase contains bracketed source restoration and rare vowels, with questionable prepositions.
Source proper names and the abbreviated reporting verb are very difficult in dense type, strong reason for independent lines.
Bottom text ends with partial `Ме-` on the printed page and must remain incomplete; no invisible footer or manuscript interpolation.
